Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 74, English)
A Live Aura-Checking Roll Call: Bhakti as "V isa," Guru's Time-Bound Grace, and Respect for Par ents

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn session consisting almost entir ely of individual, one-on-one aura-checking for dozens of named practitioners, interspersed with two substantive teaching moments — a "bhakti is a visa" analogy about time-bound grace, and a r eflection on r especting aging par ents (pr ompted by a young practitioner's visible humility towar d his own par ents). Because the overwhelming majority of this session is live, individual back-and-forth rather than conventional lectur e, Part I her e documents the session's context, format, and r ecurring patterns rather than pr esenting number ed doctrine — consistent with the adapted appr oach used for similarly structur ed sessions. In line with Ashaeiynn's own stated policy of not publicly exposing individuals' specific negativity , pitru, or tantra details, this document deliberately generalizes the aura-check content rather than listing each named practitioner's individual r eading; a small number of illustrative, non-sensitive examples ar e included by way of pattern, and one particularly personal account has been generalized further out of car e for the individual involved.
1. Session Context and Purpose

Bhaiya opens by framing the purpose of publicly sharing aura-check outcomes: encouraging honesty and openness so that others witnessing genuine improvement are moved to take up Ram Naam themselves ("sach aur saanch ko aanch nahi" — truth needs no shielding). He states that across all aura-checking done so far , only one or two people out of roughly 98% saw no improvement, and he wants this track record made visible as testimony to his own guru's devotion.
2. Format of the Session

The session consists of Bhaiya calling out practitioners' names one at a time, asking each whether they feel a dif ference since starting jaap/sadhna, then of fering a live, individualized reading — covering the presence or absence of negativity , pitru (ancestral) influence, tantra ef fects, chakra status, and specific practical guidance (jal vidhi, diya count, continued jaap, or an in-person visit when needed).
3. Recurring Positive Pattern: Marked Impr ovement With Consistency

Per this teaching, the overwhelming majority of practitioners checked in this session reported meaningful improvement — several explicitly described "180-degree" dif ferences, restored connection with Bhaiya/the divine, resolved physical ailments (e.g., discontinued long-term back pain medication), and opened chakras, generally correlated with consistent daily jaap.
4. Recurring Distinction: Negativity vs. Pitru vs. Tantra

Per this teaching, these three influences are consistently treated as distinct and independently diagnosed for each person — some practitioners were told they had no negativity but lingering ancestral (pitru) influence in the home; others had tantra ef fects without negativity; others had a mix requiring dif ferent remedies (jal vidhi for pitru-related pressure, continued jaap and diya count for negativity , and household-level attention for tantra rooted in the home rather than the individual).
5. The Direct Corr elation Practitioners Themselves Report Between Consistency and Relief

Per this teaching, several practitioners specifically noted a same-day or next-day correlation between missing jaap and feeling worse, and between doing jaap and feeling immediately better — of fered by Bhaiya as evidence that the practice itself is doing genuine, trackable work rather than being a matter of blind faith.
6. A Case of a Positive, Divinely-Guided Life Change

Per this teaching, one practitioner described how , without prior planning, she happened to encounter Bhaiya's own teaching on diet at the exact time she had independently been considering starting a specific health-related discipline — of fered as a live example of how connection to Ashaeiynn manifests through everyday , seemingly coincidental guidance.
7. Bhaiya's Own Time Constraints and Sense of Urgency

Per this teaching, Bhaiya candidly notes that he personally has only a limited window of "seva" (service) granted by his own guru, and that every subtle body (sookshma sharir) has its own allotted time; he expresses ur gency to complete his guru's assigned work "as soon as possible" precisely because this window will not last indefinitely , even while devoting whatever daily hours he can (often just an hour or so amid a very full schedule).
8. Teaching: Bhakti as a "V isa" — Time-Bound Access to Astral Power

Per this teaching's central metaphor , when a practitioner prays for bhakti, they are ef fectively asking their guru/ista devta for a "time period" ("visa") during which they can access and use astral-world abilities; once that granted time period ends, no amount of prior attainment or experience can be "carried home" — described through the vivid image of a person who worked and thrived in a foreign country for years on a visa, only to find none of that prior success transferable once the visa itself expires and re-entry becomes impossible.
9. Why This Teaching Recommends Asking Specifically for "Anany Bhakti"

Per this teaching, because bhakti functions as this time-bound access, the wisest and most enduring request to make of one's guru/ista devta is not for specific powers or outcomes but for "anany bhakti" (exclusive, unwavering devotion) — since this is what continually renews and extends the "visa," keeping the door to astral ability open, rather than requesting isolated powers that become useless once the underlying access period lapses.
10. A Brief Interlude: Playful Banter Amid the Roll Call

Per this teaching's live texture, the roll call is periodically interrupted by lighthearted, joking exchanges among sangat members and Bhaiya himself — including teasing about someone's singing voice, requests for turns to be moved up the queue, and general affectionate banter — illustrating that the session's serious spiritual work coexists comfortably with genuine warmth and humor .
1 1. Teaching: Respect for Elders as a Living Sign of Spiritual Health

Prompted by witnessing a capable young practitioner's visible humility and deference toward his own parents live during the session, Bhaiya of fers an extended reflection: that a person who remains humble before parents despite their own accomplishments carries genuine inner strength ("jhukta hai us ◌ी mein jaan hoti hai, akad to murde ki pehchaan hoti hai" — bowing carries true life; rigidity is the mark of the lifeless).
12. Why Par ents "Age" Emotionally , Not Just Chr onologically

Per this teaching, Bhaiya observes that parents do not grow old purely by number of years — they remain vital as long as they feel needed (e.g., still cooking for a grown child); the moment a child repeatedly signals independence in a way that makes a parent feel
unnecessary , this is what causes genuine emotional aging and a sense of purposelessness, more than age itself.
13. Bhaiya's Br oader Reflection on What He Witnesses in Families

Per this teaching, Bhaiya notes that he encounters an enormous range of family dynamics through his role — from genuinely warm, respectful relationships to accounts of real neglect or even harmful intentions toward aging parents — but observes that in his experience, no parent, however mistreated, ever wishes actual harm upon their own child; the reverse dynamic (children wishing ill on parents) is what he describes witnessing with far greater sadness.
14. Why Bhaiya Personally Values Hearing Everyone's Individual Experience

Per this teaching, Bhaiya explains his consistent practice of engaging personally with each practitioner's story , framing it as a natural extension of the underlying spiritual connection between every member of the sangat and Ashaeiynn's guru lineage — not simply administrative check-ins, but a genuine expression of relationship.
15. Household-Level Guidance Alongside Individual Readings

Per this teaching, in addition to individual aura readings, Bhaiya regularly extends guidance to a practitioner's household as a unit — noting when pitru influence or tantra ef fects are present in a family home rather than in any one individual, and of fering practical remedies (jal vidhi, sustained diya counts, prayers directed at ancestral influence) as ongoing household-level practice.
16. When In-Person Attendance Is Recommended

Per this teaching, for cases involving deeper -rooted household tantra or long-standing negativity that hasn't fully resolved through remote guidance and jaap alone, Bhaiya sometimes recommends an in-person visit for more direct, hands-on resolution — citing precedent from at least one other practitioner whose case had similarly required this before fully clearing.
17. A Difficult Personal Account, Handled With Car e

Per this teaching, one practitioner shared an unusually dif ficult personal history involving early-life adversity , which Bhaiya's live reading appeared to independently confirm; consistent with Ashaeiynn's stated policy against publicly exposing distressing personal details, this account is intentionally not narrated further here beyond noting that it was received with evident care, and that Bhaiya of fered reassurance regarding both the practitioner's protection going forward and the specific family blessing (kul devta) still needed to fully resolve financial and other lingering dif ficulties.
18. Closing Reassurance: Consistent Grace for Committed Practitioners

Per this teaching's closing exchanges, Bhaiya repeatedly reassures practitioners nearing the end of the roll call that Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace has never failed to respond to sincere invocation of his name, and that lingering pitru-related ef fects will continue to ease gradually with sustained prayer and practice — closing the session with a general call to continue jaap and take Bhagwan's name.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Across all aura-checking conducted so far , roughly 98% of practitioners report meaningful, trackable improvement — of fered as visible evidence of the practice's genuine ef fect. Negativity , pitru influence, and tantra are treated as distinct diagnoses requiring dif ferent remedies (continued jaap and diya count for negativity , jal vidhi and prayer for pitru pressure, household-level attention for tantra rooted in a family home). Missing jaap even briefly is often felt the very next day by consistent practitioners — of fered as direct, trackable evidence the practice is doing real work.

Bhakti functions like a time-bound "visa" granting access to astral abilities; once that granted time ends, prior attainment cannot be carried forward — the wisest request is for "anany bhakti" (unwavering devotion) itself, since this is what renews and extends that access. Every subtle body (sookshma sharir), including Bhaiya's own, has a limited allotted window of service — a reason for ur gency in completing assigned spiritual work rather than delay . Genuine humility toward parents, regardless of a person's own accomplishments, is treated as a sign of real inner strength, not weakness. Parents "age" emotionally more from feeling unneeded than from chronological years — continued small acts of being needed (e.g., a parent still cooking for a grown child) keep them vital. In this teaching's experience, no parent — however mistreated — genuinely wishes harm on their own child; the reverse pattern is what causes Bhaiya the greater sadness. Household-level guidance (pitru, tantra remedies) is of fered alongside individual readings, since these influences often af fect a family as a unit rather than one person alone. Deeply personal or distressing individual accounts shared during aura-checking are handled with care and are not exhaustively detailed here, consistent with Ashaeiynn's own privacy policy . Q1. Why does Bhaiya publicly shar e aura-check outcomes rather than keeping them private one-on-one? A: No — per this teaching, remaining humble before parents despite one's own accomplishments is described as carrying genuine inner strength; rigidity , not humility , is described as "the mark of the lifeless."

Q1 1. Per this teaching, what actually causes par ents to "age" emotionally? A: Per this teaching, feeling unneeded — not chronological years — is what causes real emotional aging in parents; continuing to let them feel needed (e.g., a parent still cooking for a grown child) keeps them vital.

Q14. Does Bhaiya offer guidance to a practitioner's household, or only to individuals? A: Both — per this teaching, householdlevel guidance is regularly extended alongside individual readings, since pitru influence or tantra ef fects often af fect a family as a unit.

Q16. How does this teaching handle a practitioner's especially difficult or distressing personal history shar ed during aurachecking? A: Per this teaching's own approach, such accounts are received with evident care but are not exhaustively detailed publicly , consistent with Ashaeiynn's stated policy against publicly exposing distressing personal details.

Q17. What closing r eassurance does Bhaiya offer practitioners toward the end of this r oll call? A: Per this teaching, that Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace has never failed to respond to sincere invocation of his name, and that lingering pitru-related ef fects will continue to ease gradually with sustained prayer and practice.
Bot Response Guidelines

Do not provide or speculate about any specific named practitioner's individual aura-check results, negativity status, pitru readings, or personal family details from this session — respond only with the general patterns and teachings documented here, consistent with Ashaeiynn's own stated privacy policy . Present the "bhakti as visa" analogy (Q6–Q7) as this teaching's own specific metaphor for time-bound spiritual access, not as a claim about literal visas or immigration. Keep the parents-related teaching (Q9–Q12) framed as this teaching's own reflection prompted by a specific live moment, not as a categorical judgment about any particular family . If asked about the "dif ficult personal account" mentioned in this session, decline to provide further detail beyond what is stated here — do not speculate about or reconstruct the specifics.
